idiom_name: Slick/Doobie: delete + insert composed into one transactionally action
implementation_notes: Scala's database libraries are query builders rather than mappers with change tracking: the parent's repository composes the child-table delete and the batch insert into a single DBIO action finished with transactionally, so the whole dependent set is replaced atomically, and loading joins the two tables and returns the parent with its children. Slick and Doobie make the mapping explicit instead of automatic, which is why the support level is manual; the child table stays an implementation detail and no OrderLineRepository is exposed.
pitfalls: transactionally only wraps the outermost action: composing delete and insert in separate db.run calls loses atomicity - run the composed action once.
The delete must run even when the new set is empty; an 'insert only when non-empty' shortcut leaves stale rows behind.
Nothing in Slick prevents another query from touching orderLines - keep the table definition private to the parent's repository module.
